<STRUCT_0001>
A fundamental insight of Michael Artin is that you can approximate
objects of a limit preserving stack. Namely, given an object <MATH_0001>
of the stack over a Noetherian complete local ring, you can find
an object <MATH_0002> over an algebraic ring which is ``close to'' <MATH_0003>.
Here an algebraic ring means a finite type <MATH_0004>-algebra and close
means adically close. In this section we present this in a simple,
yet general form.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
To formulate the result we need to pull together some definitions from
different places in the Stacks project. First, in
Criteria for Representability, Section <REF_0001>
we introduced <TEXTITOPEN_0001>limit preserving on objects<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> for <MATH_0005>-morphisms
of categories fibred in groupoids over the category of schemes.
In More on Algebra, Definition <REF_0002>
we defined the notion of a <TEXTITOPEN_0002>G-ring<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>. Let <MATH_0006> be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let <MATH_0007> be an <MATH_0008>-algebra. We say that <MATH_0009> is <TEXTITOPEN_0003>of finite type over <MATH_0010><TEXTITCLOSE_0003>
or is a <TEXTITOPEN_0004>finite type <MATH_0011>-algebra<TEXTITCLOSE_0004> if <MATH_0012> is of finite type.
